titulo.alumno: «Già, ancora e appena»: placing actions in time

intro: Master the use and exact placement of the time adverbs già, ancora and appena with compound tenses.

palabras.significado: to have just; a moment ago
kept or set aside in advance
I get off or I come down

piezas.titulo: Time values of già, ancora and appena
texto: **Già** indicates that an action has already happened or been completed: **Ho già mangiato** (I've already eaten); **Hai già prenotato?** (have you already booked?).

**Ancora** with a negation means «not yet»: **Non sono ancora pronto** (I'm not ready yet); **Non è ancora arrivato** (he hasn't arrived yet). In affirmative sentences it means «still»: **Sei ancora qui?** (are you still here?).
**Appena** means «to have just» or «a moment ago»: **Sono appena arrivata** (I've just arrived).

In compound tenses such as the passato prossimo, these adverbs are usually placed between the auxiliary and the participle: **Ho già visto quel film**; **È appena partito**; **Non ha ancora risposto**.

filas.texto: Abbiamo già comprato i biglietti. (We've already bought the tickets.)
Non ho ancora finito il lavoro. (I haven't finished the work yet.)
Il treno è appena arrivato. (The train has just arrived.)
Abiti ancora a Milano? (Do you still live in Milan?)

piezas.titulo: At the entrance to the restaurant

frases.estudio: Ciao, Elena! Hai già prenotato il tavolo per la cena di stasera?
frases.alumno: Hi, Elena! Have you already booked the table for dinner this evening?

frases.estudio: Sì, l'ho prenotato stamattina: ho riservato un posto tranquillo all'interno.
frases.alumno: Yes, I booked it this morning: I've kept a quiet spot inside.

frases.estudio: Perfetto! E Luca e Sara sono già arrivati al locale?
frases.alumno: Perfect! And have Luca and Sara already arrived at the place?

frases.estudio: No, non sono ancora arrivati: Luca mi ha scritto che è appena uscito dall'ufficio.
frases.alumno: No, they haven't arrived yet: Luca texted me that he has just left the office.

piezas.titulo: Vocabulary: temporal states, immediacy and completed processes

pregunta.texto: Which adverb is used to indicate that an action has just been carried out a few moments ago?

opciones.explicacion: «Essere / avere + appena + participle» expresses the immediacy of the action just completed.
«Già» shows that the event happened earlier, without the nuance of extreme immediacy.

pregunta.texto: Where is the adverb «già» preferably placed in a compound tense such as the passato prossimo?

opciones.texto: Placed between the auxiliary and the past participle: «Ho già visto».
opciones.explicacion: The middle position between auxiliary and participle is the most usual and natural.

opciones.texto: Always at the very beginning of the sentence before the subject.
opciones.explicacion: An emphatic position, but not the ordinary one.

opciones.texto: Joined into a single word at the end of the participle.
opciones.explicacion: It is not attached to compound verb forms.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the adverb for «to have just arrived».

frase.texto: Scusa il ritardo: sono ___ arrivata in stazione e scendo dal treno.

opciones.explicacion: «Sono appena arrivata» translates exactly as «I have just arrived».
With an affirmation it would mean that they are still arriving.
It does not give the nuance of an action just completed at this moment.

pregunta.texto: What does the construction «non ... ancora» communicate?

frase.texto: Non abbiamo ancora ricevuto la risposta formale dal comune.

opciones.texto: That the official reply is still pending and has not been received so far.
That the reply was received and filed several months ago.
opciones.explicacion: The negation with ancora confirms that it is still pending.

opciones.texto: That the reply was flatly rejected by the company.
opciones.explicacion: It does not judge the content, only the temporary absence of receipt.

pregunta.texto: What does the question with «già» ask?

frase.texto: Hai già finito di preparare la valigia per la partenza?

opciones.texto: Whether the packing of the luggage is already finished by now.
opciones.explicacion: «Già finito» asks about the completed state of the task.

opciones.texto: Whether they intend to buy a new suitcase next year.
opciones.explicacion: It asks about the current task.

opciones.texto: How many suitcases are left to check in at the terminal.
opciones.explicacion: It does not ask for counts of luggage.

frase.texto: Sono appena arrivata a casa dopo il lavoro

piezas.traduccion: I've just got home after work.
piezas.explicacion: Expression of immediate action with «appena» between auxiliary and participle.

pregunta.texto: How do you answer «have you eaten yet?» negatively, saying «not yet»?

opciones.explicacion: Standard temporal negative structure with «non ... ancora».
«Già» is not combined in this way to deny a pending state.
It would mean «I'm not just finishing eating».
